convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom('Oracle',...) which is a custom indicator with unknown internal logic. Also includes external #include <TradeAlgorithms.mqh> for trade management. Custom indicator buffers must be manually reimplemented in Python.

other_exits: Signal-based close: long closed on sell signal when BuyPosClose=true; short closed on buy signal when SellPosClose=true

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MM parameter: negative values interpreted as fixed lot size, positive as deposit fraction

custom_logic_notes: Three algorithm modes selectable via Mode enum: (1) 'breakdown' - signal line crosses zero; (2) 'twist' - signal line changes direction (compares 3 consecutive values); (3) 'disposition' - signal line crosses main line. Default mode is 'twist'. Entry signals only evaluated on new bar or when Recount=true. Recount flag set on CopyBuffer failure. LoadHistory() called each tick. SignalBar=1 means signals are read from the previous completed bar (shift 1). Permission booleans (BuyPosOpen, SellPosOpen, BuyPosClose, SellPosClose) act as gatekeepers for each trade direction and action.
python_conversion_notes: Must reverse-engineer or obtain the Oracle indicator source code to reimplement its two buffers (main=buffer0, signal=buffer1) in Python. The Oracle indicator takes params: period=55, applied_price=PRICE_CLOSE, smooth=8, recount=true. Without the Oracle indicator source, the signal generation logic is a black box. TradeAlgorithms.mqh must also be examined to understand BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose implementation details (likely standard market order execution with SL/TP and deviation handling). The three entry modes are straightforward once Oracle values are available. SignalBar=1 means using the prior bar's values - standard for backtesting. MM=-0.1 means fixed 0.1 lot sizing.
